items.evidence: Already strong after S0-S8; no new gap.
EG1 exact enumeration detected 12/12 single-predicate omission mutants versus 1/12 bounded-example detection.
EG2 certified minimum 7 resources for all current P0 NX7 slots and exposed 6 equally minimal solutions; greedy happened to be optimal on cardinality.
EG3 showed wide overlapping small-n uncertainty behind 5/5 vs 4/5 selector point rates.
EG4 shows several live frontiers blocked by missing venue, carrier, credential, observer-diversity or human outcome evidence rather than cognition.
EG5 finds repeated simulator role but owner-specific state/transition/oracle semantics.
Agent adversary and deterministic mutation search have different search distributions and authority; no universal adversary layer earned.
EG6 separates human consequence claims from mechanical/Agent judgments.
EG7 global and owner-scoped top-10 expected-source hit rates were 0.667 and 0.667; generic FTS did not beat the authority-routing baseline enough to earn a new persistent entity.
items.placement: retain Git/rg/owner authority routing; disposable indexes remain experimental

items.evidence: No stable routing law was needed to obtain EG1-EG7 benefits; per-workload placement remains clearer and cheaper.

nextPressure: Spend the next capability budget first on observation/resource acquisition, independent verification, and calibrated estimation where live owner work is blocked; use optimizers/simulators as owner-local instruments rather than new control planes.
worldModelUpdate: Agent-first remains a local design principle where Agent cognition has comparative advantage. The system-level principle is problem-first comparative capability ecology: assign each responsibility to the entity type whose properties match the invariant, then keep authority with the native owner.
